title: Software Development Practices in Kasa
description: Five text-first lessons teaching reliable debugging, test design, refactoring, Git workflow and project documentation. Executable code uses only core Kasa; Git and README activities remain external practices, not interpreter features.

units.title: Debug a program with a trace
units.goal: Locate and correct a logic error by tracing values before changing code.
units.concept: Debugging starts with a reproducible failure and a prediction. This example sums stock quantities using a loop; record the index and running total at each step. A later exercise introduces a wrong loop bound.
units.source:
ma stock = [4, 6, 3]
ma total = 0
ma i = 0
bere_a i < tentɛn(stock)
    ma total = total + stock[i]
    ma i = i + 1
awiei
ka total
trace: Define expected output 13 before running the sample.
Record total as 4, then 10, then 13 while i advances.
After three iterations i is 3, and the loop correctly stops.
units.task: Deliberately change i < tentɛn(stock) to i <= tentɛn(stock). Record the resulting error and repair the bound. Explain which input exposed the bug.
acceptance: Reproduces the failure before fixing it.
Uses a trace or observed error rather than guessing.
Restores the correct loop guard without changing sample values.
units.question: Why is changing the expected output a bad fix for an indexing bug?
units.answer: It conceals the defect instead of correcting the invalid index access.
units.complexity: Tracing each of n input items costs O(n) time.
units.mode: Core Kasa debugging; no special debugger required.

units.title: Design meaningful test cases
units.goal: Specify normal, boundary and invalid-input cases before trusting output.
units.concept: Testing checks behavior against expected results. Exact output comparisons are one useful test, but a single example does not prove correctness for all inputs. The sample handles empty lists by returning a count of zero.
units.source:
ma scores = [5, 9, 2]
ma count = 0
ma i = 0
bere_a i < tentɛn(scores)
    sɛ scores[i] >= 5 a
        ma count = count + 1
    awiei
    ma i = i + 1
awiei
ka count
trace: Define the rule: count scores greater than or equal to 5.
Confirm the expected count 2; then test zero-length and all-below-threshold inputs.
units.task: Run with [] and [1, 3, 4], expecting 0 for each. Then try [5, 5] expecting 2. Write a three-row test matrix with expected and actual results.
acceptance: Tests an empty list and a boundary value of 5.
Records actual results and compares with expectations.
Recognizes that passing examples is not proof of universal correctness.
units.question: What is a boundary test for the condition scores[i] >= 5?
units.answer: A score equal to 5, because it sits exactly on the acceptance boundary.
units.complexity: One pass through n scores costs O(n) time.
units.mode: Core Kasa runtime examples; manual test-matrix workflow.

units.title: Refactor repeated logic into a function
units.goal: Make repeated calculation logic reusable without changing behavior.
units.concept: A refactor changes structure while preserving behavior. A small named function can make intent clearer, but the best refactor is checked against the same inputs and expected outputs.
units.source:
dwumadie total_price(quantity, unit_price)
    sanma quantity * unit_price
awiei
ma first = total_price(3, 8)
ma second = total_price(2, 5)
ka first
ka second
trace: The function accepts quantity and unit price.
Two calls reuse one rule; the output remains independently checkable.
units.task: Rename the function and add a third call with quantity 0. Verify that the first two outputs have not changed.
acceptance: Uses a named function for repeated work.
Retains expected output for the original two cases.
Tests a zero-quantity case rather than assuming it works.
units.question: How do you know a refactor preserved behavior?
units.answer: Run the same inputs before and after the change and compare the outputs and relevant error behavior.
units.complexity: Each multiplication is O(1); two calls use constant work.
units.mode: Core Kasa functions; no module system required.

units.title: Plan changes with version control
units.goal: Describe a safe Git branch, commit, test and review workflow for Kasa projects.
units.concept: Git commands run in a terminal, not in the Kasa code editor. The runnable exercise models a checklist as ordinary Kasa Boolean values. A real workflow requires an external Git installation and a repository.
units.source:
ma tested = nokware
ma reviewed = nokware
ma documented = nokware
sɛ tested ne reviewed ne documented a
    ka "Ready for review"
anyɛ_saa_a
    ka "Finish checks first"
awiei
trace: Model three independent review gates as Boolean values.
All three are true, so the first branch runs.
Set reviewed to atoro and confirm the alternative message; these variables do not call Git.
units.task: Change reviewed to atoro and predict the result. Separately, outline these terminal commands: git switch -c feature/name, git add, git commit, git status. Explain why checks precede merging.
acceptance: Distinguishes Kasa sample logic from real Git commands.
Explains the purpose of a branch, commit and review.
Demonstrates that an incomplete gate prevents the ready message.
units.question: Does this Kasa program create a Git commit?
units.answer: No. It only simulates a release checklist; Git is a separate tool run outside the Academy editor.
units.complexity: Checking three Boolean gates takes O(1) time.
units.mode: Core Kasa checklist demo; terminal Git commands are conceptual.

units.title: Document and verify a small project
units.goal: Write a short project README, state assumptions and check a concrete output.
units.concept: A reproducible project specifies inputs, commands, expected outputs and limitations. The Kasa example computes a reorder decision using an explicit threshold. Documentation is created separately as a README, not generated automatically by this program.
units.source:
ma available = 4
ma reorder_limit = 6
sɛ available < reorder_limit a
    ka "Reorder stock"
anyɛ_saa_a
    ka "Stock sufficient"
awiei
trace: The program accepts available quantity 4 and reorder limit 6.
Because 4 is less than 6, it prints Reorder stock.
Document that equality (6 versus 6) means Stock sufficient; test it explicitly.
units.task: Write a README covering purpose, input assumptions, how to run the source and outputs for available=4 and available=6. Then modify the program to verify both cases.
acceptance: Documents run steps and known limitations.
Tests a below-threshold and an equal-threshold case.
Makes no claim of automatically storing inventory or writing external files.
units.question: Why should a README include exact expected output?
units.answer: It helps another person reproduce the result and notice when behavior changes.
units.complexity: One comparison and branch takes O(1) time.
units.mode: Core Kasa threshold example; README is a separate project artifact.
